clue.text: Heading away from perils, knowing crew would be thankful for this

definitions.text: crew would be thankful for this

indicators.note: the heading, or first letter, of the word goes away

parts.note: plights are perilous situations
hip means knowing, well informed

explanation.surface: Steering clear of danger, sailors who know the hazards would be grateful for such a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading away from' drops the P of PLIGHTS, leaving LIGHTS. The whole clue also reads as a description of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A moored vessel carrying a beacon to warn shipping off sandbanks, so sailors are grateful for it.

clue.text: Garden flower left out of bed at home

parts.note: someone out of bed is up
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A flower that has escaped its bed and is left lying at the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' looks like the flower bed of the surface, but 'out of bed' simply means awake.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall spiky plant with pea-like blooms, a common border plant in gardens.

clue.text: Dashes up cracking joke, struggling for breath

indicators.note: one piece cracking another breaks into it, so it sits inside

parts.note: a gag is a joke

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: nips are quick dashes, as in nipping to the shops

explanation.surface: Someone rushing about while telling a joke ends up out of breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dashes' looks like a verb of running, but it is the noun: quick trips, as in nipping out. 'up' reads that word bottom to top, giving SPIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone panting and gulping air is fighting to breathe, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Pretty-pretty birdsong abruptly terminated

indicators.note: cut off suddenly at the end, so the final letter of the word goes

parts.note: a tweet is a small bird's chirp

explanation.surface: A sweet little bird's song is suddenly cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abruptly terminated' removes the last T from TWEET.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean affectedly dainty or quaint, overly cute in a sentimental way; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Two ways to express love for author

parts.note: an embrace is one way to show affection
O is love, the zero score in tennis, and also the kiss-and-hug cross sign

explanation.surface: A writer is praised by two different expressions of affection.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase gives both pieces: a HUG, and O for love (tennis nil, or the hug in XO).
explanation.definitionFit: Victor of that surname was the French novelist who wrote Les Misérables, so this is a writer's name.

clue.text: Took a spin, arranging trip with short detour around Spain

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the other piece
arranging letters puts them in a new order
short means cut off at the end, losing the final letter

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A traveller turned around, rearranging a journey with a brief detour round Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the R of detour; 'arranging' shuffles TRIP and DETOU into PIROUTTED, which goes 'around' E.
explanation.definitionFit: A dancer who spun on one foot or on point has taken a spin.

clue.text: Cavalry getting thin time on recall

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: poor can mean thin or meagre

explanation.surface: A cavalry unit gets a meagre time when remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on recall' turns POORT round.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of mounted soldiers is called by this name, so it stands for a body of cavalry.

clue.text: Like couple in final clue touring large part of the globe

indicators.note: going round something, so the words enclose the other piece

parts.note: the final clue is 24-down, Remove a couple of fellows..., where couple is the third word

explanation.surface: A pair from the last clue travels around a big area of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: The last clue printed is 24-down, whose third word is 'couple'. 'touring' puts L inside THIRD WORD.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated term for the developing nations, a large region of the globe.

clue.text: Currency linked to half of continent a key part of problem

indicators.note: only one half of the word is kept, the other three letters going

parts.note: Europe is a continent
the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: A currency connected with part of a continent is central to some problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' keeps OPE, the back half of EUROPE.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics the quantity an operation acts upon is an essential element of a sum or problem.

clue.text: Envisaged a Parisian coming in as I quit flat

indicators.note: the French article enters the other word
I quitting means that letter leaves the word

parts.note: to envisage is to picture
un is French for a

explanation.surface: Someone imagined a Parisian arriving just as they left their apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment but is the tyre sense. 'I quit' removes I from PICTURED; UN 'coming in' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyre that has been pierced and lost its air is flat.

clue.text: Old bird pens going spare, distributed with energy

indicators.note: letters distributed are spread out in a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Pens of a long-gone bird are going spare and handed out energetically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' shuffles PENS GOING SPARE plus E. 'going spare' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This North American bird, once in vast flocks, became extinct in 1914, so it is a bird of the past.

clue.text: See 23
One of 4 divisions, 6 failing to start before storm

indicators.note: the first letter is lost, the word not getting going

parts.note: 6-across is TROOP, and a squad is a similar body of soldiers
to storm is to rant

explanation.surface: One of four sections, with the troop not starting before a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' refers to the answer at 6-across, a troop; a synonym SQUAD loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A circle or plane split into four equal parts gives quarter sections, each one of the four.

clue.text: Political affiliation of naive type?

parts.note: green means naive or inexperienced, and a party can be a person, so a naive person is a green one; also an environmentalist political group

explanation.surface: Which political group would an innocent, inexperienced person join?
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'naive type' as green (inexperienced) party (person), which is also the name of the environmentalist political group.
explanation.definitionFit: An environmentalist political organisation, which here doubles as a whimsical name for an inexperienced individual.

clue.text: What might make spaniel run from Labrador, perhaps?

indicators.note: asks what the letters could be rearranged to form

explanation.surface: Something that might send a spaniel fleeing from a Labrador dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labrador' looks like the dog alongside the spaniel, but it is the Canadian landmass. 'What might make' shuffles SPANIEL RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Labrador is a large Canadian landmass almost surrounded by sea, so anything from there belongs to such a landform.

clue.text: Man seeking apprentice, they say, to thresh crop

parts.note: Alan Sugar is the businessman who hires a winner on the TV show The Apprentice

indicators.note: signals that the next word is spoken, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: to thresh is to beat

explanation.surface: A businessman looking for a trainee is said to beat the crop.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Sugar is the boss on the British TV show The Apprentice.
explanation.definitionFit: A root vegetable grown on farms for refining into sweetener, so it is an arable crop.

clue.text: Conservative wittered on after Socialist leader took off

indicators.note: the Conservative pieces come after the Socialist one
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to witter on is to talk at length aimlessly, to ramble

explanation.surface: A Tory talked on and on after the left-wing leader left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took off' looks like a departure but is the fighter-pilot sense of hurrying into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: When military pilots scramble, they hurry aircraft into the air in an emergency.

clue.text: Stranger used to feed livestock without using force

indicators.note: the letter for force is left out

parts.note: fodder is food for farm animals
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: An outsider feeds cattle without resorting to violence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranger' looks like a noun but is the comparative of strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative adjective: more peculiar or unusual is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Dock, wiping sailor's brow

indicators.note: wiping something off removes it from the word

parts.note: to dock a text is to shorten or abridge it
AB, able seaman, is a common abbreviation for a sailor

explanation.surface: At the harbour, someone mops a seaman's forehead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dock' and 'brow' look like harbour and forehead; they mean shorten and hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: The brow of a hill is its crest, a long raised line of high ground.

clue.text: French scorer was first up — digs not good

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read upwards

parts.note: to have led is to have been first

indicators.note: not good means the letter for good is dropped

parts.note: digs are gibes, cutting remarks

explanation.surface: A French goal-scorer came top but found the lodgings poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scorer' means one who writes musical scores, not goals; 'digs' are jibes, not lodgings. 'up' reads 'was first' upwards as DEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Léo Delibes was the French composer of the ballet Coppélia, so he wrote musical scores.

clue.text: Utopian plan son's told tales about

parts.note: an idea is a plan

indicators.note: the fibbing word goes around the letter for son

parts.note: to tell tales is to lie
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A perfect scheme that a son fibbed about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'son's' is son has: S sits inside LIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something presented as perfect, better than reality, is visionary and utopian in quality.

clue.text: Quite a few leavers distraught

indicators.note: letters that are upset are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A good number of people departing are upset about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Means more than two but not many, a moderate number.

clue.text: Sign the French display on motorway?

indicators.note: in an across clue, placed on means coming after the motorway

parts.note: MI, read as M1, is Britain's principal motorway
le is French for the
to post a notice is to display it

explanation.surface: A sign the French put up on a major road.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the main motorway from London to the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside marker giving the distance to somewhere is a kind of sign.

clue.text: Passionate duck ignores duck of another kind

indicators.note: the word passes over the letter, leaving it out

parts.note: to duck something is to avoid it
in cricket a duck is a score of zero, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: An eager duck snubs a different species of duck.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket duck is a score of nought, the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Being keen and enthusiastic about something is a synonym for being passionate.

clue.text: Tenor replaces middle bit of risqué song

indicators.note: the central letter of the word is swapped out for the abbreviation for tenor

parts.note: something risqué is dirty or rude

explanation.surface: A tenor substitutes the middle verse of a naughty song.
explanation.definitionFit: A short simple tune or comic song is a light kind of song.

clue.text: Scotsman's swallowed up by one marine creature or another

indicators.note: the creature takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: a seal is a sea mammal

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read upwards

parts.note: Ian is a typically Scottish name, so Ian's is the Scotsman's

explanation.surface: A Scot is eaten by one sea animal or perhaps a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads the Scotsman's name upwards as SNAI. 'another' is the definition: a second marine creature, after the one in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A marine gastropod mollusc, so it is a further sea creature beyond the seal.

clue.text: Remove a couple of fellows after a party

indicators.note: the fellows come after the party

parts.note: a do is a party
F is the abbreviation for fellow, so two of them give FF

explanation.surface: Taking something off after a party with two men.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off a hat or garment is a dated synonym for removing it.

clue.text: Man from party carried me to ball, transformed

indicators.note: transformed letters change their form into a new order

explanation.surface: A man from a party carried someone to a dance and changed them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' looks like the ball, but it is a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the UK centrist political party formed in 1988 is a man from that party.

clue.text: Dim working dog departs for far side of ranch

indicators.note: one letter stands in for another

parts.note: a husky is a sled-pulling working dog

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is meant

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A slow-witted working dog leaves for the far end of the farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Shadowy and dark in colour, as at twilight, so faint or dim.

clue.text: By implication, some not quite exuding calm?

definitions.text: By implication, some not quite exuding calm?

parts.words: By implication, some not quite exuding calm?
parts.note: if some only partly give off calm, by implication the remainder do so completely; also the plain sense of in a calm way

explanation.surface: If some people are not entirely serene, what follows about others?
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as REST FULLY: if some are not quite calm, the rest are fully so, and the whole word means in a tranquil manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Means in a calm and soothing manner, peacefully.
